correctness.rationale: For every nonempty support S, closed NOR is exactly the product of complementary row and column support sets. This gives F cubed equals F and identifies every periodic rectangle. Inclusion–exclusion computes H(r,c), giving exact individual basin sizes and the distinguished basin B. Bonferroni bounds on jointly empty rows and columns prove a uniform vanishing relative-error asymptotic; the proof handles empty S and 2-by-2 boundary boards. Re-execution from the packaged Python and C++ source agrees on 169,808 and 1,676,112 labelled board configurations, respectively, but is not presented as an all-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: A full attraction-basin classification, including all individual orbit fibers, is a natural invariant for this infinite two-parameter canonical family. The unique giant basin holds uniformly across every board and its exceptional measure changes from an \(a2^{-b}\) mechanism in elongated boards to an \(ab2^{-(a+b-1)}\) mechanism in balanced boards. The sharp \(b\asymp2^{a-1}\) scaling clarifies how two correlated missing-axis events interact. The finding goes beyond a single finite census; its significance does not depend on downstream claims or external certification.
